answer_parts.text: The change occurred starting with WebSphere Application Server V8.0. Beginning with V8.0 and all subsequent releases and fix packs, one install package contains updates for both WebSphere Application Server and the Java SDK; applying a WebSphere fix pack also upgrades the bundled SDK. Separate Java SDK-only fix packs remained available.

For WebSphere V7.x, fix packs were still installed using the Update Installer, while Installation Manager was used for certain V7 feature-pack installations and maintenance. The evidence specifically describes installing the SCA feature pack on WAS V7.0.0.7 or later by first applying the WAS fix pack with Update Installer, then using Installation Manager for the feature pack and its fix packs.

answer_parts.text: The default SSP provider derives the SSP URL from the RES URL supplied to Decision Center by replacing the application name with `testing`; it therefore assumes the SSP is reachable through the same host and port. There is no separate standard port setting described for this default behavior.
To point DVS to a different application server, create a custom SSP resolver, package it in `teamserver.war`, and set the `teamserver.defaultSSPResolver.class` property to that class.
Implement `IlrSSPResolver.getSSPURL(String serverName, URL url)` so it returns the desired SSP URL, such as `http://runtime-host:9000/testing`, based on the configured server name.

Define separate servers in Decision Center/RTS with their RES URLs, then have the resolver map each server name to its corresponding SSP URL; DVS execution is dispatched according to the server selected for the test.
The SSP must contain the required XOMs and be deployed with an XU connection factory and the appropriate datasource.

answer_parts.text: The IBM Security Bulletin for IBM Integration Bus and WebSphere Message Broker is the relevant source. It covers the FREAK (Factoring Attack on RSA-EXPORT keys) TLS/SSL vulnerability, CVE-2015-0138.

The vulnerability could let a remote man-in-the-middle attacker downgrade certain SSL/TLS connections and facilitate brute-force decryption of traffic when an IBM SSL/TLS client accepts an RSA temporary key in a non-export RSA key-exchange cipher suite.
Affected products listed are IBM Integration Bus V9 and V10, IBM Integration Bus Toolkit V9, and WebSphere Message Broker V7 and V8, including the corresponding Toolkit versions.

For the bulletin and remediation information, use the IBM support links cited in the bulletin: IBM Integration Bus V10 fixes are in fix pack 10.0.0.1 via http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg24040056; IBM Integration Bus V9 and WebSphere Message Broker V7/V8 interim fixes are available through IBM Fix Central; and Toolkit fixes are linked from the bulletin.
The bulletin identifies APARs IT07823 and IT07802 for IBM Integration Bus, IT07736 for WebSphere Message Broker, and IT07802 for the Toolkit fixes. It lists no known workarounds or mitigations.
The CVSS base score is 4.3, with vector AV:N/AC:M/Au:N/C:N/I:P/A:N; the bulletin directs readers to IBM X-Force for the current temporal score.

answer_parts.text: The IBM bulletin specifically covering IBM Integration Bus and WebSphere Message Broker is titled “Multiple vulnerabilities in IBM Java Runtime affect IIB and WMB (CVE-2015-0138).” Its summary states that the bulletin addresses multiple IBM SDK Java vulnerabilities and the “FREAK: Factoring Attack on RSA-EXPORT keys” TLS/SSL client and server vulnerability.

For the vulnerability details and fixes, consult IBM’s related bulletin “Vulnerability with RSA Export Keys may affect IBM WebSphere Application Server (CVE-2015-0138)” at http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21698613. The bulletin also references the IBM Java SDK January 2015 CPU at http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21695362.

CVE-2015-0138 is a vulnerability in IBM SSL/TLS implementations that could allow a remote attacker to downgrade certain SSL/TLS connections. An IBM SSL/TLS client could accept an RSA temporary key in a non-export RSA key-exchange cipher suite, enabling a man-in-the-middle attacker to facilitate brute-force decryption of TLS/SSL traffic.
This vulnerability is also known as the FREAK attack. Its CVSS base score is 4.3, with vector (AV:N/AC:M/Au:N/C:N/I:P/A:N).

IBM recommends installing the interim fix for APAR IT07386 for the current IBM Business Process Manager or WebSphere Lombardi Edition version; Fix Central links are provided for the Express, Standard, Advanced, and WebSphere Lombardi Edition products.
IBM also provides My Notifications at http://www-01.ibm.com/software/support/einfo.html for future security-bulletin alerts.

valid_parts.text: For the vulnerability details and fixes, consult IBM’s related bulletin “Vulnerability with RSA Export Keys may affect IBM WebSphere Application Server (CVE-2015-0138)” at http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21698613. The bulletin also references the IBM Java SDK January 2015 CPU at http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21695362.

CVE-2015-0138 is a vulnerability in IBM SSL/TLS implementations that could allow a remote attacker to downgrade certain SSL/TLS connections. An IBM SSL/TLS client could accept an RSA temporary key in a non-export RSA key-exchange cipher suite, enabling a man-in-the-middle attacker to facilitate brute-force decryption of TLS/SSL traffic.
This vulnerability is also known as the FREAK attack. Its CVSS base score is 4.3, with vector (AV:N/AC:M/Au:N/C:N/I:P/A:N).

IBM recommends installing the interim fix for APAR IT07386 for the current IBM Business Process Manager or WebSphere Lombardi Edition version; Fix Central links are provided for the Express, Standard, Advanced, and WebSphere Lombardi Edition products.
IBM also provides My Notifications at http://www-01.ibm.com/software/support/einfo.html for future security-bulletin alerts.

answer_parts.text: On HP-UX, verbose GC is not written to a log file by default; configure it in the server’s generic JVM arguments.
Add these generic JVM arguments: -XX:+PrintGCDetails, -XX:+PrintGCDateStamps, -XX:+PrintHeapAtGC, and -Xverbosegc:file=/tmp/gc_pid$$.vgc.
The $$ placeholder maps to the Java process PID, so the output file is created with a PID-specific name.
To enable rotation, also add -XX:+UseGCLogFileRotation, -XX:NumberOfGCLogFiles=10, and -XX:GCLogFileSize=10M.

answer_parts.text: IBM Tivoli Network Manager IP Edition Version 4.2.0.1 is downloaded through the Passport Advantage Online Web site. Log in, select “Software download & media access,” choose “Download finder,” select “Find by product description,” search for “Tivoli Network Manager,” expand the Tivoli Software eAssembly, and select the required images.

For AIX, the required part number is CNE9WEN — IBM Tivoli Network Manager IP Edition 4.2.0.1 for AIX. It includes the base product, core components, GUI components, and topology database scripts.

The documented supported platforms include AIX 6.1 and 7.1 on PowerPC systems, and Red Hat Enterprise Linux 6 or 7 (x86-64) and SLES 11.0 (x86-64) on Intel/AMD systems.

valid_parts.text: IBM Tivoli Network Manager IP Edition Version 4.2.0.1 is downloaded through the Passport Advantage Online Web site. Log in, select “Software download & media access,” choose “Download finder,” select “Find by product description,” search for “Tivoli Network Manager,” expand the Tivoli Software eAssembly, and select the required images.
For Linux, the required part number is CNE9VEN — IBM Tivoli Network Manager IP Edition 4.2.0.1 for Linux. It includes the base product, core components, GUI components, and topology database scripts.

The multilingual Quick Start Guide part is CNE9UML. DB2 10.5 Enterprise Server Edition for Tivoli Netcool/OMNIbus, Network Manager, and Netcool Configuration Manager is listed as part CRYY2ML.

To install, download all required and any needed optional parts, unpack each part into a single temporary directory, and follow the IBM Knowledge Center installation instructions or the IBM Tivoli Network Manager IP Edition V4.2 Quick Start Guide.
The documented supported platforms include AIX 6.1 and 7.1 on PowerPC systems, and Red Hat Enterprise Linux 6 or 7 (x86-64) and SLES 11.0 (x86-64) on Intel/AMD systems.

answer_parts.text: IBM Tivoli Network Manager IP Edition Version 4.2 Fix Pack 1 (V4.2.0.1) is available through the Passport Advantage Online Web site. Log in, select “Software download & media access,” choose “Download finder,” select “Find by product description,” search for “Tivoli Network Manager,” expand the Tivoli Software eAssembly, and select the required images.
The documented download package is “Download Network Manager 4.2.0.1 for AIX and Linux,” released on 22 September 2016, with HTTPS download available through Passport Advantage.

For the multilingual V4.2.0.1 installation, the required Linux part number is CNE9VEN: IBM Tivoli Network Manager IP Edition 4.2.0.1 for Linux. It contains the base product, core components, GUI components, and topology database scripts.
The required AIX part number is CNE9WEN: IBM Tivoli Network Manager IP Edition 4.2.0.1 for AIX. It contains the base product, core components, GUI components, and topology database scripts.
Other listed parts include CNE9UML, the V4.2.0.1 Quick Start Guide, and CRYY2ML, IBM DB2 10.5 Enterprise Server Edition for Tivoli Netcool/OMNIbus, Network Manager, and Netcool Configuration Manager.

To install, download all required and any needed optional parts, unpack each part into a single temporary directory, and follow the Installing section of the IBM Knowledge Center. The installation instructions also direct users to the IBM Tivoli Network Manager IP Edition V4.2 Quick Start Guide.
The documented supported platforms include AIX 6.1 and 7.1 on IBM PowerPC-based systems, and Red Hat Enterprise Linux 6 or 7 and SLES 11.0 SP2/SP3 on Intel or AMD x86-64 systems.
The Network Manager V4.2 publication library is available in IBM Knowledge Center at https://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/SSSHRK_4.2.0/itnm/ip/wip/common/welcome.html.

answer_parts.text: Adding the replacement certificate to the Validation Credential does not necessarily make DataPower use it. DataPower configuration ultimately references specific certificate files, and existing configuration continues using the old files until the Crypto Key and Certificate objects are updated to reference the replacements.
If the replacement certificate uses the same filename as the expired certificate, disable and re-enable the certificate object to clear cached references to the expired certificate.

Also verify that the complete certificate chain is installed, including the personal, intermediate, and root certificates where applicable; newer certificates are often chained and are not always a one-for-one replacement.

If the Validation Credential contains both the old and new CA certificates with the same subject Distinguished Name, older DataPower firmware searches by subject DN and may select the first certificate—the expired one—causing validation to fail. Use only one certificate for a given subject DN in the Validation Credential, or upgrade to firmware above 3.8.1.

answer_parts.text: The supplied documentation does not identify a CICS JVMSERVER-specific cause for remaining in the “BEING DISABLED” state. It does document that a JVM server can fail to initialize its OSGi framework and then be terminated, leaving the JVMSERVER disabled when the Language Environment enclave was not created; this can occur when required zFS files were not propagated to the target environment.

A separate documented hang mechanism is an application-server JVM thread becoming stuck while logging an FFDC incident. Hung-thread notifications appear as WSVR0605W messages, and if the FFDC thread never completes, the condition behaves like a true deadlock and can require server cancellation.
For refreshing a Java program running in a JVM server, the documented procedure is to disable and then enable the JVMSERVER resource.

answer_parts.text: The MQ v8 client’s AMS support checks for an AMS security policy when it opens a queue. This check can occur even when the queue is not AMS-protected, and the AMS component does not need to be actively in use.

For the described MQ v8 client/MQ v7 server combination, the relevant failure is an AMS policy lookup/parsing problem on the client side, rather than a requirement that the remote queue manager have AMS installed. The documented exception for this class of problem is MQRC 6114 (MQRC_INSUFFICIENT_DATA).

The documented workarounds are to use MQ v8 classes for JMS/Java, use MQ v7.5.0.4 classes with AMS disabled, or remove the AMS component from the client installation if the connecting applications do not require it.
For MQ v7.5 Java/JMS classes, the defect was fixed in maintenance level 7.5.0.6.

answer_parts.text: A possible cause is an abnormal queue-manager termination, such as a sudden reboot, followed by recovery of a queue containing a mixture of persistent and non-persistent messages. This can damage the queue or cause previously retrieved persistent messages to reappear.

The documented failure sequence involves putting persistent messages, flushing them to disk outside a checkpoint, retrieving them all, initiating a checkpoint, putting a non-persistent message before the queue is checkpointed, and then hard-crashing the queue manager.

To determine whether this occurred, check whether the queue is reported as damaged when accessed. IBM Service can examine the queue file; a typical damaged queue is 1712 bytes or, more likely, 10240 bytes, with a non-null message-chain head but no message.

The queue-checkpoint logic was revised to correct this problem. Fixes are listed for WebSphere MQ 6.0.2.12, 7.0.1.10, 7.1.0.3, and 7.5.0.1, with platform-specific maintenance details provided in the APAR.

valid_parts.text: A queue manager that ends abnormally—for example, after a sudden machine reboot—may, during restart recovery, leave a damaged queue or cause previously retrieved persistent messages to reappear.

To investigate, check whether the queue is reported as damaged when accessed. A typical damaged queue may be 1712 bytes or, more likely, 10240 bytes; IBM Service can examine the queue file for a non-null message-chain head with no message.

The queue-checkpoint logic was revised to correct this problem. Fixes are available in WebSphere MQ 6.0.2.12, 7.0.1.10, 7.1.0.3, and 7.5.0.1, with platform-specific fix details listed for the affected releases.

answer_parts.text: The relevant information is in IBM’s Security Bulletin about the “FREAK: Factoring Attack on RSA-EXPORT keys” TLS/SSL vulnerability. The bulletin identifies the issue as CVE-2015-0138—not CVE-2015-0118—and explains that vulnerable IBM SSL/TLS clients could accept an RSA temporary key in a non-export RSA cipher suite, enabling a man-in-the-middle attacker to facilitate brute-force decryption of TLS/SSL traffic.
The bulletin covers IBM Integration Bus V9 and V10, IBM Integration Bus Toolkit V9, WebSphere Message Broker V7 and V8, and WebSphere Message Broker Toolkit V7 and V8.

For remediation, consult the listed APARs and fix links: IIB V10—IT07823 and IT07802 in fix pack 10.0.0.1; IIB V9—IT07823 and IT07802; IIB Toolkit V9—IT07802; WMB V8—IT07736; WMB Toolkit V8—IT07802; WMB V7—IT07736; and WMB Toolkit V7—IT07802.

The bulletin states that no workarounds or mitigations are known. It also provides IBM’s Secure Engineering Web Portal and Product Security Incident Response Blog as related information sources, and recommends subscribing to My Notifications for future security bulletins.

answer_parts.text: The CPU spike occurs when the MQ Queue Manager object has Retry Attempts set to 0. That setting disables the Long Retry Interval, so DataPower retries indefinitely using the configured Retry Interval; the defaults are 0 attempts and a 1-second retry interval for backward compatibility.

Resolve it by changing Retry Attempts from 0 to a finite number in the DataPower MQ Queue Manager configuration. One example is Retry Attempts = 6, Retry Interval = 10 seconds, and Long Retry Interval = 600 seconds (10 minutes).
With that example, DataPower retries six times at 10-second intervals when the queue manager is down, then retries every 10 minutes.
A separate high-CPU issue is documented for MQ Sharing Conversation: customers using MQ Sharing Conversation can get high CPU, and a fix is available in DataPower 7.1.0.7.

For older DataPower firmware releases 7.0.0.x, 7.1.0.x, 7.2.0.x and earlier, the Sharing Conversations guidance is to use a negotiated value of 0; configuring values of 1 or more may cause reloads or hangs due to connection instability and generate MQ reason codes 2009 and 2059.

answer_parts.text: The CPU spike occurs when the DataPower MQ Queue Manager object is configured with Retry Attempts set to 0. That setting disables use of the Long Retry Interval, so DataPower retries indefinitely using the configured Retry Interval. The defaults—0 retry attempts and a 1-second retry interval—are retained for backward compatibility but should be changed to use the Long Retry Interval feature.

Resolve the issue by changing Retry Attempts from 0 to a finite number in the Configure MQ Queue Manager window. One example is Retry Attempts = 6, Retry Interval = 10 seconds, and Long Retry Interval = 600 seconds (10 minutes).
With that example, if the queue manager is down or the connection cannot be established, DataPower retries six times at 10-second intervals and then retries every 10 minutes.

answer_parts.text: The supplied IBM bulletin for CVE-2016-1000031 concerns Apache Commons FileUpload vulnerabilities affecting IBM WebSphere Service Registry and Repository (WSRR).

The vulnerability is a critical remote-code-execution issue caused by deserialization of untrusted data in the FileUpload library’s DiskFileItem class. It has a CVSS 3.0 base score of 9.8, with vector CVSS:3.0/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H.
Affected versions listed are WebSphere Service Registry and Repository V8.5 and V8.0.

For remediation, apply fixes for both IBM WebSphere Application Server and IBM WebSphere Service Registry and Repository. The WebSphere Application Server bulletin is available at http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg22011428.
For WSRR, the vulnerability was fixed under APAR IJ01131; fixes are available from IBM Fix Central. For WSRR V8.5, apply V8.5.6.1_IJ01131.
For WSRR V8.0, apply the listed V8.0.0.3 fix containing IJ01131, available through IBM Fix Central.
The bulletin was originally published on 04 January 2018. IBM’s security bulletin portal is available at http://www.ibm.com/security/secure-engineering/bulletins.html.

valid_parts.text: The supplied IBM bulletin for CVE-2016-1000031 concerns Apache Commons FileUpload vulnerabilities affecting IBM WebSphere Service Registry and Repository (WSRR).

The vulnerability is a critical remote-code-execution issue caused by deserialization of untrusted data in the FileUpload library’s DiskFileItem class. It has a CVSS 3.0 base score of 9.8, with vector CVSS:3.0/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H.
Affected versions listed are WebSphere Service Registry and Repository V8.5 and V8.0.

For remediation, apply fixes for both IBM WebSphere Application Server and IBM WebSphere Service Registry and Repository. The WebSphere Application Server bulletin is available at http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg22011428.
The bulletin was originally published on 04 January 2018. IBM’s security bulletin portal is available at http://www.ibm.com/security/secure-engineering/bulletins.html.

answer_parts.text: The message means the upgrade could not preserve the appliance’s user-modified data because there was insufficient flash space to install the firmware image; consequently, the firmware image was not installed and the system will not reboot as part of that failed installation.
Before retrying, save the current configuration and create a backup of the entire system, storing it off the appliance.
Remove the appliance from production, remove extraneous files, reboot the appliance to release temporary storage, then transfer and install the firmware image according to the upgrade documentation.

Temporary space includes the user-accessible temporary, image, export, and logtemp directories; temporary and internal space are also used for processing, and some displayed space is occupied by internal files and a rollback image that are not visible to the user.

Review the version-specific DataPower upgrade documentation before proceeding, and ensure that you have a working admin account plus a backup privileged account that can change the admin password if needed.
If the space cannot be freed or the upgrade continues to fail, contact IBM Support using the standard DataPower appliance support process.

The supplied documentation does not identify an ODR OutOfMemoryError introduced specifically by WAS version 8553 or by unchanged configuration and traffic conditions.

answer_parts.text: The requested IBM PureApplication System bulletin is documented in the supplied security bulletin. It describes CVE-2015-1920 in the bundled WebSphere Application Server: a remote attacker could execute arbitrary code by connecting to a management port and following a specific sequence of instructions. The CVSS base score is 9.3, with vector AV:N/AC:M/Au:N/C:C/I:C/A:C.
For additional vulnerability details, consult IBM’s “Security Vulnerability in IBM WebSphere Application Server” bulletin: http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21883573
The affected PureApplication System versions listed are V2.1, V2.0, and V1.1; the WebSphere Application Server bundle is included in the Web Application Pattern.
For remediation, IBM lists Web Application Pattern Type V2.0.4.2 and V1.0.4.2 for PureApplication System V2.1, available through IBM Fix Central links in the bulletin.
For PureApplication System V2.0, upgrade to V2.0.0.1 Interim Fix 5. For V1.1 and earlier, contact IBM customer support for upgrade options.

The bulletin lists no workaround or mitigation. IBM My Notifications can be used for future security-bulletin alerts, and related information is available through IBM’s Secure Engineering Web Portal and Product Security Incident Response Blog.

answer_parts.text: The IBM PureApplication System bulletin states that IBM WebSphere Application Server contains a vulnerability allowing a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code by connecting to a management port and executing a specific sequence of instructions.
For the detailed vulnerability information, consult IBM’s bulletin “Security Vulnerability in IBM WebSphere Application Server” at http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21883573.
The bulletin identifies CVE-2015-1920, with a CVSS base score of 9.3 and vector (AV:N/AC:M/Au:N/C:C/I:C/A:C).
Affected products listed are IBM PureApplication System versions 2.1, 2.0, and 1.1.

Fix information is provided through IBM Fix Central: for version 2.1, apply Web Application Pattern Type 2.0.4.2 or 1.0.4.2; for version 2.0, upgrade to version 2.0.0.1 Interim Fix 5; for version 1.1 and earlier, contact IBM customer support for upgrade options.

The bulletin identifies CVE-2015-1920, with a CVSS base score of 9.3 and vector (AV:N/AC:M/Au:N/C:C/I:C/A:C).
Affected products listed are IBM PureApplication System versions 2.1, 2.0, and 1.1.

answer_parts.text: The documented resolution for this type of hung-thread condition is to tune the `es-workmanager` thread-pool size. Its defaults are a minimum of 2 threads, a maximum of 20, and Growable set to true; if the maximum has been limited, performance tuning may be needed to prevent blocked threads. Test the tuning in a pre-production environment first.

The underlying cause is that event sequencing calls `startWork`, which blocks until work is placed in the thread pool. If no thread is available, the call can remain blocked indefinitely and WSVR0605W warnings accumulate.
Configure the work manager in the administrative console at Resources > Asynchronous beans > Work managers > es-workmanager.

If the hang occurs while stopping an application containing a resource adapter, a separate WebSphere Application Server deadlock defect may be involved; the J2C synchronization fix was targeted for fix packs 7.0.0.35, 8.0.0.10, and 8.5.5.3.

answer_parts.text: The documented cause is a deadlock between the application-stop thread and the J2C resource-adapter work thread performing a lookup; synchronization issues can prevent the application from stopping.
This issue is associated with WebSphere Application Server fix pack levels that include APAR PM93319.

Resolve it by applying a WebSphere Application Server fix pack containing the correction. The fix was targeted for WebSphere Application Server 7.0.0.35, 8.0.0.10, and 8.5.5.3; later listed fix packs are also available, including 7.0.0.45, 8.0.0.15, and 8.5.5.13.
The correction updates WebSphere Application Server J2C code to properly synchronize the locking objects.
The APAR documentation lists no local or temporary fix.

answer_parts.text: The error means the process exhausted its available file handles, including sockets, so new sockets or file descriptors could not be opened.

A common cause is a file-descriptor leak in part of the application. In this deployment-related case, deployment code may not have been cleaned up after an application upgrade or uninstall, leaving old EAR files held open by WebSphere components and requiring a server restart to clear them.
Another possible cause is a system configuration limit: on UNIX/Linux, the process ulimit for file handles may be set too low for the application’s file and socket usage.

answer_parts.text: The “Too many open files” error means the process has exhausted its available file handles, including sockets, so it cannot open new sockets or file descriptors. In most cases, this is caused by file handles being leaked by part of the application; it can also result from a system configuration limit that is set too low.

If the deployment was running on Windows with DataStage, a specific cause is that MKS Toolkit did not have enough free file locks for the number of DataStage jobs running. Its default maximum of 255 active file locks may need to be increased, for example to 300, followed by a Windows server restart.
On UNIX/Linux, check the process file-handle limits (`ulimit -Sn` and `ulimit -Hn`); the default limit may be too low, although increasing it does not prevent errors caused by file-descriptor leaks.

answer_parts.text: IBM WebSphere MQ 7.0 and later support the SVRCONN channel SHARECNV attribute, which sets the maximum number of conversations sharing each TCP/IP channel instance. DataPower negotiates its configured value with the MQ server, and the lower value takes effect.

For DataPower firmware 7.0.0.x, 7.1.0.x, 7.2.0.x, and earlier, use a negotiated value of 0. Configuring case 2 or case 3 on those firmware versions may cause reloads or hangs and MQ reason codes 2009 and 2059.
For firmware 7.5.0.x, 7.5.1.x, and later, cases 2 and 3 can be used. The documentation suggests configuring 10 or less and empirically verifying that the MQ server can sustain the resulting load.

To disable conversation sharing regardless of the SVRCONN setting, configure Sharing Conversations as 0 or 1 on the DataPower mq-qm object. DataPower treats a configured value of 1 as 0 during negotiation in current firmware versions.

Use value 1 when each TCP/IP channel instance should have one conversation while retaining MQ 7-or-later features. Configure Sharing Conversations to 1 and Share Single Conversation to on in DataPower, and set the MQ SVRCONN value to 1.
The Share Single Conversation attribute is displayed only when Sharing Conversations is set to 1 and the Return key is entered; it is hidden for values greater than 1.
Use a value of 2 or more on both the DataPower mq-qm object and the MQ SVRCONN channel when each TCP/IP channel instance should support at least two conversations.

Because DataPower uses a connection pool, sharing conversations generally provides no additional benefit. An exception is mixed message sizes on the same mq-qm object, where case 2 can benefit from MQ 7 buffer management and Read Ahead; case 1 uses the maximum configured message size as the MQGET buffer pool.
Before using sharing conversations, apply APAR IV24821 to the MQ server; it is included in MQ 7.0.1.10 and later, 7.1.0.3 and later, 7.5.0.1 and later, and MQ 8.

valid_parts.text: IBM WebSphere MQ 7.0 and later support the SVRCONN channel SHARECNV attribute, which sets the maximum number of conversations sharing each TCP/IP channel instance. DataPower negotiates its configured value with the MQ server, and the lower value takes effect.

For DataPower firmware 7.0.0.x, 7.1.0.x, 7.2.0.x, and earlier, use a negotiated value of 0. Configuring case 2 or case 3 on those firmware versions may cause reloads or hangs and MQ reason codes 2009 and 2059.
For firmware 7.5.0.x, 7.5.1.x, and later, cases 2 and 3 can be used. The documentation suggests configuring 10 or less and empirically verifying that the MQ server can sustain the resulting load.

To disable conversation sharing regardless of the SVRCONN setting, configure Sharing Conversations as 0 or 1 on the DataPower mq-qm object. DataPower treats a configured value of 1 as 0 during negotiation in current firmware versions.
The Share Single Conversation attribute is displayed only when Sharing Conversations is set to 1 and the Return key is entered; it is hidden for values greater than 1.
Use a value of 2 or more on both the DataPower mq-qm object and the MQ SVRCONN channel when each TCP/IP channel instance should support at least two conversations.

Because DataPower uses a connection pool, sharing conversations generally provides no additional benefit. An exception is mixed message sizes on the same mq-qm object, where case 2 can benefit from MQ 7 buffer management and Read Ahead; case 1 uses the maximum configured message size as the MQGET buffer pool.

answer_parts.text: Use conversation sharing only when appropriate for your DataPower firmware and workload. DataPower uses a connection pool, so sharing conversations generally provides no additional benefit; however, with mixed message sizes, case #2 (negotiated value 1) can benefit the mq-qm object through MQ Version 7 buffer management and Read Ahead.

For DataPower firmware 7.0.0.x, 7.1.0.x, 7.2.0.x and earlier, use a negotiated sharing-conversations value of 0. Configuring case #2 or #3 on those releases may cause reloads or hangs due to connection instability.

Cases #2 and #3 are supported for firmware 7.5.0.x, 7.5.1.x and later. IBM suggests using 10 or less in the DataPower Sharing Conversations attribute and empirically verifying that the MQ server can sustain the negotiated load.
The negotiated value is the lower of the DataPower mq-qm value and the MQ SVRCONN SHARECNV value. DataPower's default is 0, while the MQ SVRCONN default is 10.
To disable sharing regardless of the SVRCONN setting, set DataPower Sharing Conversations to 0 or 1. In current DataPower firmware, a configured value of 1 is treated as 0 during negotiation.

For a negotiated value of 1, set DataPower Sharing Conversations to 1, select Share Single Conversation = on, and set the MQ SVRCONN value to 1. The Share Single Conversation attribute appears only when Sharing Conversations is set to 1 and Return is pressed; it is hidden for values greater than 1.
For a negotiated value of 2 or more, set Sharing Conversations to 2 or more on both the DataPower mq-qm object and the MQ SVRCONN channel.
Before using sharing conversations, apply MQ APAR IV24821; it is included in MQ V7.0.1.10 and later, V7.1.0.3 and later, V7.5.0.1 and later, and MQ V8.

valid_parts.text: Use conversation sharing only when appropriate for your DataPower firmware and workload. DataPower uses a connection pool, so sharing conversations generally provides no additional benefit; however, with mixed message sizes, case #2 (negotiated value 1) can benefit the mq-qm object through MQ Version 7 buffer management and Read Ahead.

For DataPower firmware 7.0.0.x, 7.1.0.x, 7.2.0.x and earlier, use a negotiated sharing-conversations value of 0. Configuring case #2 or #3 on those releases may cause reloads or hangs due to connection instability.

Cases #2 and #3 are supported for firmware 7.5.0.x, 7.5.1.x and later. IBM suggests using 10 or less in the DataPower Sharing Conversations attribute and empirically verifying that the MQ server can sustain the negotiated load.
To disable sharing regardless of the SVRCONN setting, set DataPower Sharing Conversations to 0 or 1. In current DataPower firmware, a configured value of 1 is treated as 0 during negotiation.

For a negotiated value of 1, set DataPower Sharing Conversations to 1, select Share Single Conversation = on, and set the MQ SVRCONN value to 1. The Share Single Conversation attribute appears only when Sharing Conversations is set to 1 and Return is pressed; it is hidden for values greater than 1.
For a negotiated value of 2 or more, set Sharing Conversations to 2 or more on both the DataPower mq-qm object and the MQ SVRCONN channel.
Before using sharing conversations, apply MQ APAR IV24821; it is included in MQ V7.0.1.10 and later, V7.1.0.3 and later, V7.5.0.1 and later, and MQ V8.

For IBM MQ V9.0 LTS, apply maintenance level 9.0.0.1; for IBM MQ V8.0, apply maintenance level 8.0.0.6.
The bulletin lists no workaround or mitigation.

You can find related security information through IBM’s Secure Engineering Web Portal and Product Security Incident Response Blog. The bulletin also links to the CVE record and IBM X-Force page for the current CVSS temporal score.

An authenticated user with queue-manager permissions could trigger a segmentation fault; normal operations might require rebooting the machine. The CVSS base score is 5.3, with vector CVSS:3.0/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H.
Affected versions are IBM MQ V9.0.0.0 in the V9.0 Long Term Support Release and IBM MQ V8.0.0.0 through V8.0.0.5 maintenance levels.
For remediation, apply maintenance level 9.0.0.1 for the V9.0 Long Term Support Release or 8.0.0.6 for IBM MQ V8.0.
The bulletin lists no workarounds or mitigations.

You can find related IBM security information through the IBM Secure Engineering Web Portal and the IBM Product Security Incident Response Blog; the bulletin also provides a Japanese translation link.

answer_parts.text: WebSphere MQ V7.0 included Java 5.0 Service Refresh 16 Fix Pack 8 (SR16-FP8). The corresponding maintenance level was V7.0.1.13.
WebSphere MQ V7.1 and V7.5 included Java 6.0. An update set them to Java 6.0 Service Refresh 16 Fix Pack 2 (SR16-FP2), with the fix targeted to V7.1.0.7 and V7.5.0.5.

A later update for WebSphere MQ V7.1 and V7.5 specified platform-dependent Java levels: Java 6.0 SR16-FP26 (6.0.16.26) on AIX, Linux x86-32/x86-64, Linux PPC64, zLinux, and Windows; SR16-FP22 (6.0.16.22) on HP-UX IA32/IA64; and SR16-FP25 (6.0.16.25) on Solaris x86-64/SPARC.

WebSphere MQ V8.0 included platform-dependent Java levels: Java 7.1 SR3-FP40 (7.1.3.40) on AIX, Linux x86-32/x86-64, Linux PPC64LE, zLinux, and Windows 32-/64-bit; Java 7.0 SR9-FP32 (7.0.9.32) on HP-UX IA32/IA64; and Java 7.0 SR9-FP40 (7.0.9.40) on Solaris x86-64/SPARC.
The supplied JRE was used by Java components including the GSKit graphical interface and WebSphere MQ Explorer; in some releases it also supported Managed File Transfer and the MQXR service.

For GSKit, the evidence identifies the affected bundled levels by MQ maintenance release rather than giving a GSKit numeric version: the issue affected GSKit included with all MQ 7.5 levels and with MQ 8.0.0.0 and 8.0.0.4, but not MQ 8.0.0.1 through 8.0.0.3. The defect fix was targeted to MQ 7.5.0.6 and MQ 8.0.0.5.

For WebSphere MQ V6.0 on Windows, the evidence states that MQ 6.0.2.1 used a Java runtime to run GSKit certificate-administration commands and that the correction was delivered in fix pack 6.0.2.2 (PTF U200270). It does not state a numeric Java JRE or GSKit version for MQ V6.0.

WebSphere MQ V8.0 included platform-dependent Java levels: Java 7.1 SR3-FP40 (7.1.3.40) on AIX, Linux x86-32/x86-64, Linux PPC64LE, zLinux, and Windows 32-/64-bit; Java 7.0 SR9-FP32 (7.0.9.32) on HP-UX IA32/IA64; and Java 7.0 SR9-FP40 (7.0.9.40) on Solaris x86-64/SPARC.

answer_parts.text: This symptom is commonly caused by incorrect permissions on the image folder, the image being outside the specified directory, or the specified image directory not existing.
For PDF/Excel generation, the image path must resolve to a physical location accessible by the dispatcher; an image existing only on the web server may not be found or accessible by the dispatcher.

Verify the image path and place the image directory in the specified location. For a relative path such as ../samples/images/pic.jpg, the dispatcher looks under <c10 install>/webcontent/samples/images/pic.jpg.

If permissions are the cause, open IIS, select the Cognos installation root, open Authentication, enable anonymous access, and repeat this for the image folder and its parent folder; then test Excel 2007 and PDF output again.
To identify the specific failure, run Process Monitor on the Cognos machine while exporting the report, filter for the image name, and inspect the Result column.

In a multi-tier environment with SSL enabled, a blank PDF image can also result from an incomplete or missing SSL Chain of Trust in the IBM Cognos keystore. The documented options are to place the images on the application tier at the same path as on the gateway, or import the SSL certificate chain into the application-tier Cognos CA keystore.
